title: Privacy of always-on XR cameras
bottleneck: Useful AR needs always-on cameras mapping surroundings and watching hands, but that means continuous recording of bystanders, homes, and workplaces. On-device processing helps, yet raw sensor data is a breach waiting to happen, and bystanders can't consent. No technical framework guarantees camera data never leaves the device or is misused.
why_it_blocks: Privacy fears could trigger regulation or social rejection that kills face-worn cameras regardless of technical merit. The most capable AR is also the most surveillant.
current_state: Vendors promise on-device processing and indicator LEDs, but these are policies, not proofs. Verifiable privacy architectures for XR sensing don't exist. Indicator lights and on-device processing promises are policies, not cryptographic guarantees, and bystanders cannot verify them. Raw camera feeds are the most sensitive data a wearable can collect, yet users have no way to audit what the device actually retains.
